name: The Stack v1
contains: One record is a permissively licensed source file from GitHub with its text, size, language, extension and the star, fork and issue counts and licenses of the repository it came from.
format: Gated HF dataset with no splits (loads as train); parquet files in one folder per language under data/, loaded with datasets.load_dataset("bigcode/the-stack", data_dir="data/dockerfile", split="train"); fields include content, size, lang, ext, avg_line_length, max_line_length, alphanum_fraction, hexsha and max_stars/forks/issues repo path, name, head hexsha and licenses.
size: Over 6 TB per the card (catalog: 6.4 TB full, 2.9 TB near-deduplicated, about 200B training tokens, taken from the Stack v3 card table)
license: Gated: acceptance of the BigCode Terms of Use is required; license:other, with permissive per-file licenses recorded in the license fields
limitations: The card warns that the dataset contains a lot of near-duplicates which can cause leakage into any custom test split. The card also says license attribution is limited by the accuracy of GHArchive and go-license-detector, and that the training data could contain malicious code.

popularity.note: The download figure is for the bigcode/the-stack repo. No recipe in data/model-recipes.json names v1.

evidence: Read the gated card (README via resolve/main, 2026-11-25): summary, data fields, data splits, limitations; HF API for downloads and likes; sizes from the catalog entry (v3 card table). Maturity: released 2022-11, still the reference baseline and cited in later BigCode releases. No model-recipes entry names it, so used_by is empty.

name: The Stack v2
contains: One record is a pointer to a source file in the Software Heritage archive (blob id, repository, path, detected licenses, license type, commit and snapshot ids, GitHub star and fork counts) whose text is fetched separately from the Software Heritage S3 bucket.
format: Gated HF dataset of metadata only (parquet under data/<language>/, one train split); one config per language plus a default config; fields blob_id, directory_id, path, content_id, detected_licenses, license_type, repo_name, snapshot_id, revision_id, branch_name, visit_date, revision_date, committer_date, github_id, star_events_count, fork_events_count, gha_license_id, gha_event_created_at, gha_created_at, gha_language, language, src_encoding, is_vendor, is_generated, length_bytes, extension; file contents are downloaded from s3://softwareheritage using the blob ids.
size: 67.53 TB uncompressed total, 3.28B unique files from 104.2M GitHub repositories (card); catalog records 32.1 TB deduplicated and a 2.0 TB, about 550B-token training subset
license: Gated: BigCode terms plus the Software Heritage and Inria agreement for bulk content download; license:other, per-file licenses in detected_licenses and license_type
limitations: The card says file contents are stored in the Software Heritage S3 bucket and bulk download requires an agreement with Software Heritage and Inria. The card also warns that the dataset contains many near-duplicates that can cause leakage into a custom test split.

popularity.note: Software Heritage related: the corpus is a view of the Software Heritage archive (2023-09-06 graph), see also catalog entry software-heritage-graph. opencoder-8b used it as 12.5% of RefineCode.

evidence: Read the gated card (README via resolve/main, 2026-11-25): summary, languages, data fields, data collection (3.28B files, 104.2M repos, 67.53 TB), download section; HF API for stats; data/model-recipes.json entries starcoder2-15b, opencoder-8b, smollm3-3b name it. Maturity: released 2024-02 and used by three 2024 to 2025 recipes.

name: StarCoderData
contains: One record is a cleaned, decontaminated, PII-redacted source file, GitHub issue thread, Jupyter notebook parsed into script or text-code form, or git commit from the StarCoder (v1) training mix.
format: Gated HF dataset with one data_dir per language (for example load_dataset("bigcode/starcoderdata", data_dir="python", split="train")) and four separate folders for jupyter-scripts-dedup-filtered, jupyter-structured-clean-dedup, github-issues-filtered-structured and git-commits-cleaned; the issues, commits and notebooks use different columns, so load them separately.
size: 783 GB of code in 86 languages plus 54 GB GitHub issues, 13 GB Jupyter notebooks and 32 GB GitHub commits, about 250 billion tokens (card)
license: Gated: BigCode terms of use; license:other, permissively licensed source
limitations: The card says loading the entire dataset at once may fail because issues, commits and notebooks have different columns than the language folders. The data is a 2022-era snapshot of The Stack, so overlap with benchmarks published after that date was not removed.

popularity.note: No recipe in data/model-recipes.json names this exact dataset.

evidence: Read the gated card (README via resolve/main, 2026-11-25): description, creation, usage, subset folder names; HF API for stats. The last limitation sentence is the catalog caveat on the 2022 cutoff (data/resources catalog id starcoderdata) rather than card text. Maturity: released 2023-05, a standard baseline.

name: StarCoder2 data extras
contains: One record is a text document with a single content field, taken from one of twelve non-code or code-adjacent sources: arXiv, code documentation, GitHub issues, Kaggle notebooks, LLVM IR, Stack Overflow, Wikipedia, OpenWebMath and others.
format: HF datasets with 12 configs (arxiv, documentation, ir_cpp, ir_low_resource, ir_python, ir_rust, issues, kaggle, lhq, owm, stackoverflow, wikipedia), each a train split with a single string column content (verified on the arxiv config with the datasets-server first-rows API).
size: Rows per config: arxiv 1,558,306; documentation 59,733; ir_cpp 2,916,655; ir_low_resource 393,988; ir_python 154,507; ir_rust 32,720; issues 15,549,682; kaggle 580,195; lhq 7,037,500; owm 6,315,233; stackoverflow 10,404,628; wikipedia 6,630,651 (card dataset_info)
license: Not stated at dataset level (HF license field unset); components carry their own terms, for example Stack Overflow under CC-BY-SA
limitations: The dataset-level license is unset, so each component (arXiv, Stack Overflow, Wikipedia, Kaggle) has to be cleared separately. Stack Overflow text is CC-BY-SA, which requires attribution and share-alike.

popularity.note: This is the documentation and Q&A source in the starter list: the documentation and stackoverflow configs hold library documentation and Stack Overflow text.

evidence: HF API cardData.dataset_info (config names and row counts) and datasets-server first-rows (field name content), fetched 2026-11-25; catalog caveats; data/model-recipes.json starcoder2-15b lists issues, pull requests, Kaggle and Jupyter notebooks, documentation and intermediate representations as sources. Maturity: released 2024-02, a documented component of StarCoder2.

name: Stack-Edu
contains: One record is a pointer to an educational-quality source file (blob id, repository name, path, language, encoding, byte length, classifier score and integer score, detected licenses, license type) whose text is fetched from Software Heritage.
format: HF datasets with one config per language (C, CSharp, Cpp, Go, Java, JavaScript, Markdown, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, SQL, Shell, Swift, TypeScript), each a train split; fields blob_id, language, repo_name, path, src_encoding, length_bytes, score, int_score, detected_licenses, license_type; file contents are downloaded from the Software Heritage S3 bucket.
size: 167,063,359 rows across 15 configs (summed from the card dataset_info); for example Java 44,990,158, Python 25,286,019, Cpp 16,246,746
license: Not stated on the card (HF license field unset); underlying files come from the permissively licensed StarCoder2Data, with per-file licenses in detected_licenses and license_type
limitations: The dataset ships blob ids and metadata only, so the file text must be downloaded from Software Heritage. Educational scores come from language-specific classifiers trained on LLM annotations, so labels near the score threshold are noisy.
evidence: HF API cardData.dataset_info (all 15 configs), datasets-server first-rows (field names), catalog caveats, fetched 2026-11-25; data/model-recipes.json olmo-3-32b and smollm3-3b name Stack-Edu. Maturity: released 2025-03 and used by two 2025 recipes.

name: CommitPack
contains: One record is a single-file commit from a permissively licensed GitHub repository with the file before and after the commit, the commit subject and message, language, repository license and repository name.
format: HF dataset with a commitpack.py loading script and per-language folders under data/, fields commit, old_file, new_file, old_contents, new_contents, subject, message, lang, license, repos, returncode, stderr.
size: 4 TB; 57,700,105 samples, 3,709,175.78 MB in the card table (largest languages by rows: markdown 7.6M, python 6.2M, javascript 5.4M)
license: MIT (card); each sample comes from a permissively licensed repository and carries its license in the license field
limitations: It is very large and noisy, and the card describes it as the unfiltered source from which CommitPackFT was derived. Commit messages are often not written as instructions, which is why the filtered CommitPackFT exists.

popularity.note: The viewer is unavailable for this repo, so field names come from the card, not the datasets-server.

evidence: Read the card (README via resolve/main, 2026-11-25): summary, data fields, data splits table, licensing; HF API for stats. The second limitation sentence combines the card description of CommitPackFT as filtered for messages resembling instructions with the catalog caveat. Maturity: released 2023 and stable.

name: GitHub Code (CodeParrot)
contains: One record is a source file from GitHub with its code, repository name, path, language, repository license and size in bytes.
languages: 30 to 32 languages (the card says 32 in the description and 30 in the Languages section)
format: HF dataset of parquet shards (data/train-*.parquet; streaming recommended), single train split; fields code, repo_name, path, language, license, size; load_dataset("codeparrot/github-code", streaming=True, split="train", languages=["Dockerfile"]) filters by language.
size: 115M files, about 1 TB (card)
license: license:other; each file keeps the license of its repository, a mix of permissive and copyleft
limitations: The files include copyleft licenses such as GPL, so a permissive-only policy needs filtering on the license field. The data was built from the public GitHub dataset on Google BigQuery and is not deduplicated, so benchmark contamination is likely.

popularity.note: There is also codeparrot/github-code-clean, a cleaned variant, in the catalog.

evidence: Read the card (README via resolve/main, 2026-11-25): description, usage, data fields, languages; HF API for stats. Contamination sentence is the catalog caveat. Maturity: released 2022, superseded by The Stack but still a common baseline.

name: RefineCode (metadata)
contains: One record is a metadata row for a file in the OpenCoder RefineCode corpus (repository name, sub path, file name, extension, size in bytes, line count, language, programming language and document type) that points back into The Stack v2.
format: HF dataset with one split named The_Stack_V2 and fields repo_name, sub_path, file_name, file_ext, file_size_in_byte, line_count, lang, program_lang, doc_type; code text must be fetched from Software Heritage.
size: 336,845,710 files in the The_Stack_V2 split (HF dataset_info)
license: MIT for the metadata; underlying code keeps its per-repository licenses
limitations: Only the Stack v2 half of RefineCode is covered, because the GitHub half was withheld for legal reasons according to the card. You still need Stack v2 and Software Heritage access to obtain any code text.

popularity.note: Used_by cites OpenCoder, which trained on the full RefineCode, of which this is the Stack v2 metadata half.

evidence: HF API dataset_info and license, datasets-server first-rows field names, catalog caveats, fetched 2026-11-25; data/model-recipes.json opencoder-8b (RefineCode 960B tokens). Maturity: released 2024-11, one recipe.
